note: rebuild Oct 29: hook re-cut and 75 s cap (IMPROVE 00a, 00c), fresh opus reviewer
reasons: 1. As an HVAC owner: most shops on ServiceTitan close about a third of their estimates and the top quarter close about 70%, so work out my own rate (jobs sold / estimates given, same month) and put those two numbers on the whiteboard every Friday.

2. Stop: yes. Frame 0.8s asks 'Do you know your close rate?' in big orange type on a whiteboard. Most owners don't know theirs, and the spoken 'Here's the one-line math' at 2.3 s promises a quick answer, so I'd give it a few seconds. It's a softer stop than last cut's 38% / 31% card because there's no number on screen yet, but it's clearer: no region card that reads like sides of a city, so last cut's map confusion is gone.

3. Send: yes, to my estimator. 'Send this to whoever writes your estimates' fits how my shop works. Save: yes. The formula, the 40 / 14 = 35% example and the Friday two-number habit are worth keeping, and 'screenshot this' lands right before the formula. Follow or link: no, not yet. One useful lesson earns a save, and 'Free tools for trade owners: link in bio' gives me no reason to tap today.

4. Hype, fake urgency, pitch, slop or robotic: nothing that would make me scroll past. No countdown, no pitch, and the caveat ('ServiceTitan doesn't say how it counts a close, and its customers aren't every shop out there') reads as honest. The AI voice is labelled (aiLabel true). A couple of lines are a little flat, e.g. 00:19.9 'That's a big gap.' and 00:33.2 'Here's an example where you gave forty estimates last month and sold fourteen.' (fix, optional: 'Say you gave forty estimates last month and sold fourteen.'). That's not blocking.

5. Unclear to a stranger, minor: 00:12.0 to 00:16.5 'top quarter of shops, ranked by close rate in each region. Their median runs seventy to seventy-three percent' is still a median of a median. It's clear enough, but 'the top quarter of shops close seventy to seventy-three percent' is easier. The caption has a dollar check ('$ sold / $ quoted') and asks 'count or by dollars?', but the voice no longer mentions dollars. They don't contradict each other, and the caption just adds a step. Fine as is.
6. Trust: yes. The source and dates are in the caption, the example checks out (35% sits inside 31 to 38%), and it tells me to beat my own last-month number instead of chasing the benchmark.

Weak spots, not blocking: on frame 0.8s the speech bubble ('Do you know your') repeats the whiteboard text, and the bottom 40% is floor and props. The key text sits high, so Reels UI won't cover it. Fix, optional: put a number teaser like '31 to 38%' somewhere in frame 0.8s to make the stop stronger.
